topics.title: WAEC marathon: algebra
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to solve quadratic equations using factorization method
The students should be able to simplify algebraic expressions
The students should be able to solve word problems involving linear equations

Introduction:
We have previously studied basic algebraic operations and equation solving. Today we will practice WAEC-style algebra questions to prepare for the examination.

Content:
Quadratic equations are equations of the form ax² + bx + c = 0. To solve by factorization we look for two numbers that multiply to ac and add to b. For example to solve x² + 5x + 6 = 0 we find 2 and 3 multiply to 6 and add to 5 so we write (x+2)(x+3)=0 giving x=-2 or x=-3. Algebraic expressions are simplified by combining like terms. For example 3x + 2x - 5y = 5x - 5y. Word problems like finding the cost of yams in the market can be set as linear equations. If yams cost ₦200 each and you buy 5 with ₦1000 remaining we write 200y + 1000 = total money.

Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to solve 10 WAEC past questions on quadratic equations and word problems within 30 minutes.

Evaluation questions:
1. Solve the equation x² - 7x + 10 = 0
2. Simplify the expression 3a²b × 2ab³
3. If a book costs ₦1500 and a pen costs ₦300, write an equation for buying 2 books and p pens with ₦5000
4. Explain the difference between an algebraic expression and an equation

Summary:
Today we practiced solving quadratic equations, simplifying expressions and setting up equations from word problems to build our algebra skills for WAEC.

topics.title: WAEC marathon: geometry
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state the circle theorems
The students should be able to construct angles and triangles using ruler and compasses
The students should be able to solve problems involving similar triangles

Introduction:
We have previously studied basic geometric shapes and properties. Today we will focus on WAEC-style geometry questions including theorems and constructions.

Content:
Circle theorems include: angles in the same segment are equal; the angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference is 90°; opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°. For construction, we use ruler and compasses to construct perpendicular bisectors, angles and triangles. To construct a 60° angle, draw a line, mark a point, draw an arc from that point, then from where the arc intersects the line draw another arc to intersect the first arc. The line from the original point to this intersection gives 60°. Similar triangles have corresponding angles equal and sides in proportion. If two triangles are similar with ratio 1:2, then all corresponding sides of the second triangle are twice as long as the first.

Class activity:
Students will practice constructing angles, triangles and perpendicular bisectors using ruler and compasses on plain paper.

Evaluation questions:
1. State two circle theorems
2. Construct an equilateral triangle with sides 6cm
3. If triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF with ratio 3:4 and AB = 9cm, what is the length of DE?
4. Explain how to construct a 90° angle using only a ruler and compasses

Summary:
Today we reviewed circle theorems, practiced geometric constructions and solved problems involving similar triangles to strengthen our geometry knowledge for WAEC.

topics.title: WAEC marathon: trigonometry
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to calculate angles using bearings
The students should be able to solve problems involving heights and distances
The students should be able to use trigonometric ratios to find unknown sides

Introduction:
We have previously studied basic trigonometric ratios and angle measurement. Today we will practice WAEC-style questions on bearings, heights and distances.

Content:
Bearings are measured clockwise from north and written as three-digit angles. For example bearing 030° is 30° clockwise from north. To solve height problems, we use trigonometric ratios. If a pole casts a 10m shadow and the angle of elevation of the sun is 45°, then height = 10 × tan(45°) = 10m. For distances, if two points A and B are on opposite sides of a river and the angle from A to B is 60° with distance 50m, we can find the width using tan(60°) = width/50. Trigonometric ratios are sinθ = opposite/hypotenuse, cosθ = adjacent/hypotenuse, tanθ = opposite/adjacent. Special values include sin30°=0.5, cos60°=0.5, tan45°=1.

Class activity:
Students will work in groups to solve five bearing problems and five height/distance problems using trigonometric ratios.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the bearing of southwest?
2. If a tree is 20m tall and casts a shadow 15m long, what is the angle of elevation of the sun?
3. A ladder leans against a wall with its base 3m from the wall. If the ladder is 5m long, how high up the wall does it reach?
4. Explain how to find the distance across a river using trigonometry

Summary:
Today we practiced calculating bearings, solving height and distance problems, and applying trigonometric ratios to prepare for WAEC trigonometry questions.

topics.title: WAEC marathon: statistics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to calculate mean, median and mode
The students should be able to construct and interpret frequency tables
The students should be able to solve probability problems

Introduction:
We have previously studied basic statistical measures and probability concepts. Today we will practice WAEC-style statistics and probability questions.

Content:
The mean is the average calculated by summing all values and dividing by the number of values. The median is the middle value when data is ordered. The mode is the most frequent value. For example in test scores 45, 52, 52, 60, 70 the mean is 458/5=57.6, median is 52, mode is 52. Frequency tables organize data into classes with their frequencies. Probability is calculated as number of favorable outcomes divided by total outcomes. For example if a bag contains 3 red balls and 2 blue balls, the probability of drawing red is 3/5. Independent events have P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B). For example the probability of rolling a 6 and flipping heads is 1/6 × 1/2 = 1/12.

Class activity:
Students will collect data on the number of siblings each student has, organize it into a frequency table, and calculate mean, median and mode.

Evaluation questions:
1. Calculate the mean of the following data: 12, 15, 18, 20, 25
2. Find the median and mode of 7, 9, 11, 9, 13, 11, 9
3. If a die is rolled, what is the probability of getting an even number?
4. Explain the difference between discrete and continuous data

Summary:
Today we practiced calculating statistical measures, constructing frequency tables and solving probability problems to strengthen our statistics skills for WAEC.

topics.title: WAEC marathon: mensuration
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to calculate the volume and surface area of solids
The students should be able to find the area of sectors and segments of circles
The students should be able to solve practical problems involving mensuration

Introduction:
We have previously studied formulas for calculating areas and volumes of shapes. Today we will practice WAEC-style mensuration questions involving solids and sectors.

Content:
The volume of a cylinder is πr²h where r is radius and h is height. Surface area is 2πr² + 2πrh. For a cone, volume is (1/3)πr²h and surface area is πr² + πrl where l is slant height. The area of a sector is (θ/360) × πr² where θ is the angle in degrees. The area of a segment is area of sector minus area of triangle. For example a sector with radius 7cm and angle 60° has area (60/360) × π × 7² = (1/6) × π × 49 ≈ 25.67cm². Practical problems include finding the volume of a water tank, the amount of paint needed to cover a cylindrical drum, or the area of land that can be irrigated from a circular sprinkler system.

Class activity:
Students will measure dimensions of classroom objects and calculate their volumes and surface areas.

Evaluation questions:
1. Calculate the volume of a cylinder with radius 3cm and height 10cm
2. Find the area of a sector with radius 14cm and angle 45°
3. A cylindrical tank has diameter 2m and height 3m. How many liters of water can it hold? (1m³ = 1000 liters)
4. Explain how to find the surface area of a cone

Summary:
Today we practiced calculating volumes and surface areas of solids and finding areas of sectors and segments to prepare for WAEC mensuration questions.

topics.title: Mock examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete a full WAEC mathematics paper under timed conditions
The students should be able to apply knowledge from all topics covered
The students should be able to manage time effectively across different question types

Introduction:
We have been practicing various topics in preparation for the WAEC examination. Today you will complete a full mock examination to assess your readiness.

Content:
The mock examination will consist of two papers: Paper 1 (objective) and Paper 2 (theory). Paper 1 has 50 multiple-choice questions to be completed in 1 hour 30 minutes. Paper 2 has 13 questions including essay problems to be completed in 2 hours 30 minutes. Questions will cover all topics including algebra, geometry, trigonometry, statistics and mensuration. You must show all working for theory questions as marks are awarded for method. Time management is crucial - spend about 1 minute per objective question and allocate time to theory questions based on marks.

Class activity:
Students will complete the full mock examination under timed examination conditions.

Evaluation questions:
The mock examination itself serves as evaluation with questions covering all topics.

Summary:
Today's mock examination provided practice under exam conditions and identified areas needing further revision before the actual WAEC examination.

topics.title: Weakness clinics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify their weak areas in mathematics
The students should be able to solve targeted problems in identified weak topics
The students should be able to develop strategies to improve performance

Introduction:
From the mock examination, we have identified areas where many students need improvement. Today we will focus on these weak areas with targeted practice.

Content:
Based on the mock examination results, common weaknesses include quadratic equations, circle theorems, trigonometric calculations, and probability problems. For quadratic equations, we will practice different solving methods including factorization, formula and completing the square. For circle theorems, we will review each theorem with examples and practice applying them to problems. In trigonometry, we will focus on bearings and height calculations with emphasis on correct use of trigonometric ratios. For probability, we will practice solving problems involving independent and dependent events with clear working. Students will work in groups based on their identified weaknesses to share strategies and solutions.

Class activity:
Students will be grouped according to their weak areas and work together on targeted problems with guidance from the teacher.

Evaluation questions:
1. Solve x² - 5x + 6 = 0 using the quadratic formula
2. State the angle subtended by an arc at the center and at the circumference
3. If a pole 6m tall casts a shadow 8m long, what is the angle of elevation of the sun?
4. Explain how to calculate the probability of two independent events both occurring

Summary:
Today we focused on individual weak areas with targeted practice to strengthen understanding and improve performance in those topics.

topics.title: Speed and accuracy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to solve mathematics problems quickly and accurately
The students should be able to recognize question patterns and select appropriate methods
The students should be able to minimize careless errors in calculations

Introduction:
As the examination approaches, we need to develop both speed and accuracy in solving problems. Today we will practice working quickly while maintaining accuracy.

Content:
Speed in mathematics comes from recognizing patterns and knowing formulas. For example recognizing that x² + 5x + 6 can be factored as (x+2)(x+3) quickly without trial and error. Accuracy comes from careful working and checking. Always write down each step of calculations rather than doing too much in your head. For objective questions, use elimination techniques to narrow down options. For theory questions, allocate time based on marks - a 3-mark question should take about 3 minutes. Practice mental arithmetic for common calculations like percentages, fractions and square roots. Track your speed and accuracy in practice sessions to identify areas for improvement.

Class activity:
Students will complete timed objective tests with immediate feedback to improve speed and accuracy.

Evaluation questions:
1. Solve 2x + 5 = 15 in 10 seconds
2. Calculate 25% of ₦1200 in 15 seconds
3. Find the next term in the sequence 2, 6, 18, 54 in 20 seconds
4. Explain how to balance speed and accuracy in examinations

Summary:
Today we practiced developing speed and accuracy in solving mathematics problems through timed exercises and recognizing solution patterns.

topics.title: Final mock
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete a full WAEC mathematics paper under timed conditions
The students should be able to apply all mathematics knowledge effectively
The students should be able to demonstrate examination readiness

Introduction:
After targeted practice on weak areas, today we will complete another full mock examination to assess improvement and final readiness.

Content:
The final mock examination will be identical in format to the actual WAEC mathematics examination with Paper 1 (objective) and Paper 2 (theory). This simulation includes the timing, question types and marking scheme of the real examination. The objective paper has 50 questions to be completed in 1 hour 30 minutes, while the theory paper has 13 questions to be completed in 2 hours 30 minutes. Questions cover all topics from the syllabus with emphasis on areas identified as challenging in previous assessments. After completion, we will review answers and discuss examination strategies for optimal performance.

Class activity:
Students will complete the full mock examination under timed examination conditions followed by group review of answers.

Evaluation questions:
The final mock examination itself serves as evaluation with comprehensive coverage of all topics.

Summary:
Today's final mock examination demonstrated improvement and highlighted final areas needing attention before the actual WAEC examination.

topics.title: WAEC readiness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate effective examination strategies
The students should be able to prepare all necessary materials for the examination
The students should be able to maintain confidence and manage examination stress

Introduction:
The WAEC examination begins next week. Today we will finalize preparation strategies and ensure all students are ready for the examination.

Content:
For examination day, arrive early with all required materials including mathematical set, ruler, pencil, eraser and approved calculator. Manage time by reading all questions first and allocating time based on marks. Start with questions you find easiest to build confidence. For objective questions, use elimination techniques to narrow down options. For theory questions, show all working as marks are awarded for method. Check calculations carefully and avoid careless errors. Maintain positive self-talk and remember that proper preparation has been done. On the night before, get adequate rest and eat properly. During the examination, stay calm and focused, reading each question carefully before answering.

Class activity:
Students will practice examination strategies through timed question drills and discuss managing examination stress.

Evaluation questions:
1. List three materials to bring to the mathematics examination
2. Explain how to allocate time during the examination
3. Describe how to manage examination stress
4. What should you do if you encounter a very difficult question?

Summary:
Today we finalized examination strategies and materials to ensure all students approach the WAEC mathematics examination with confidence and proper preparation.
